source.ref: Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, Sch. Art. 20(1) (subst. by Act 07 of 2016 w.e.f. 1-4-2016)
source.quoted_text: Sch Art. 20(1) (both columns): 'For Conveyance — as defined by clause (d) of section 2, not being a transfer charged or exempted under No.52, on the market value of the property which is the subject matter of conveyance — five percent of the value.' This is the BARE Art 20(1) rate (5% of market value), the canonical cross-ref target for 'same duty as a conveyance under Article 20(1)' (gift non-family, lease clause (vi), exchange, etc.). It carries NO s.3B cess — cross-refs import the charge only; each referring rule adds its own cess where the s.3B list applies.

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: HIGH (official DPAL text). The bare 5% Art 20(1) rate. Rebaseable via cross_ref `on` (it is a plain ad_valorem), so lease (vi) can apply it to max(lease_base, market_value) and gift to property value. Kept separate from KA-ART20-conveyance (which adds the first-sale concession + s.3B cess) so the cross-ref chain is clean — mirrors Delhi's stamp-only conveyance-rate pattern.

source.ref: Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957, Sch. Art. 20(1) & (2A) (subst. by Act 07 of 2016 w.e.f. 1-4-2016)
source.quoted_text: Sch Art. 20 (both columns, official DPAL text): '20(1) ... five percent of the [market] value. (2A) where an instrument of conveyance relating to the FIRST SALE of flat or apartment — (i) where the market value is rupees twenty lakhs or less — two percent of the value; (ii) where above rupees twenty lakhs but upto and inclusive of thirty five lakhs — three percent of the value.' Plus s.3B additional infrastructure duty (10% of the stamp duty) — see modifier.

pending_verification.reason: MISSING BAND — Act 26 of 2021 (in force at once, 05-10-2021) inserted Art 20(2A)(iii): "where the market value of which is above rupees thirty five lakhs but upto and inclusive of forty five lakhs | three percent of the value". We encode bands only to 35 lakh, so a first-sale flat between 35L and 45L falls through to the 5% residual and is OVERCHARGED by two percentage points — the most common retail transaction in the state, wrong since Oct 2021. Untouched by Act 04 of 2024, so the band is live today. KA-SOURCING.md logged this as a DISCREPANCY resolved in favour of our primary; the secondaries were right and the primary was stale.

notes_for_reviewer: CONFIDENCE: HIGH for the stamp rate (official DPAL); MEDIUM for the surcharge (secondary, corroborated). Conveyance = 5% + s.3B 10%-of-duty cess (0.5%) + local surcharge (2% urban / 3% rural of duty) = 5.6% urban / 5.65% rural. FIRST-SALE flat (fact first_sale_flat=yes): ≤Rs 20L → 2%; >20L≤35L → 3%; >35L → 5%. DISCREPANCY (primary followed): some secondary sources call 2/3/5 a general value slab capped at Rs 45L, but Art 20(2A) confines 2%/3% to FIRST SALE of a flat, capped at Rs 35L. Reg fee (1%) is a separate adjunct (M3).
